title: Microflow Investigator: lightweight request thread inspector for cost-aware tracing
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design and prototype a compact, in-context request thread inspector (Microflow Investigator) for the Redwood Console that lets engineers rapidly pivot from a request list to a lightweight per-request view showing spans, correlation IDs, timeline scrubber, and per-span cost estimates. Goal is a low-friction drilldown that preserves the primary trace context (service lanes, request meta) while surfacing actionable signals: hot spans, tail latency contributors, cache hits, and cost attribution to model tokens and external calls.
background: Current Request Details is a heavy modal with full trace canvas that takes time to load and is hard to scan for cost-causing spans. Support tickets and customer interviews show engineers want a fast, scannable inspector to decide whether to open the full trace. This design explores a compact, side-rail microflow that is accessible from lists and dashboards, optimized for quick triage and low latency on load.
acceptance_criteria: Microflow opens from request list with <300ms perceived latency in prototype (mocked backend)
Shows top 6 spans by duration and top 3 by cost with contextual metadata (service, op, correlation IDs)
Timeline scrubber allows jumping to a span and expands full trace only when user requests 'Open full trace'
Per-span cost is computed and displayed (token estimate + external call cost) and matches engineering's sample calc within 10%
Supports filter-by-correlation-id copy and 'open in timeline' deep link to full trace view
UX passes 5/6 participants in 20-minute usability sessions for rapid triage tasks
engineering_notes: Prototype uses mocked span index; ENG backlog items ENG-23411 (span-summary API) and ENG-23412 (per-span-cost calc) must land before beta
We recommend a minimal JSON payload: request_meta + top_spans[] with aggregated metrics to reduce list-to-inspector payload size
Fallback behavior: if span index missing, show top-level request metrics and 'expand to full trace' CTA
Accessibility: timeline scrubber must be keyboard operable and announce current timestamp/selected span
decisions: Keep Microflow as a dismissible ephemeral side panel rather than modal to preserve dashboard context
Limit initial span list to 6 to keep inspector compact; allow 'show more' to expand to full trace canvas
Surface cost estimates inline rather than hidden in detail panel to accelerate cost triage
tradeoffs: Compact view reduces context compared to full trace but improves perceived load time and scan speed
Estimating cost client-side from token heuristics is faster but may diverge from actual billing by small amounts; we accept delta within 10% for triage purposes
Keeping the side panel ephemeral avoids navigation cost but requires careful focus management for accessibility
usability_findings: 5 researchers tested 12 engineers; median time-to-decision reduced from 2m20s (full trace) to 38s with Microflow
Participants liked the explicit per-span cost badges and correlation-id quick-copy; confusion arose around 'cache hit' icon semantics and will be iterated
One participant expected keyboard shortcut from request list; propose Ctrl+Shift+I to open focused inspector (engineering to validate conflicts)
